questions.question: Which cloud targets should the probe run against?

options.label: S3 general-purpose
options.description: Your existing live bucket, under a probe prefix that gets cleaned up. Settles the S3 `//` point.

options.label: S3 directory bucket
options.description: A temporary Express One Zone bucket, created, probed and deleted by the script. Settles every directory-bucket point. Needs permission to create buckets.

options.label: Azure (live account)
options.description: Your ADLS Gen2 (HNS) account, plus a flat-namespace account if you have one. Settles the Azure `.`, `..`, `//`, `\` points.

options.label: Graph
options.description: The graph_live tenant: CON.txt, a.txt next to A.txt, dot segments, trailing `/`. Leave unticked if you'd rather not touch that tenant.

questions.question: Should the local Docker stack (MinIO, Azurite, OpenSSH) be probed too?

options.label: Yes, as a labelled column (Recommended)
options.description: It settles nothing about the authorities, but it shows where the emulators the conformance tests run against differ from the real service.

options.label: No, cloud only
options.description: Keeps the doc to authoritative measurements. Any emulator divergence stays unknown.

questions.question: Where should the probe and its results land?

options.label: In PR #1173 (Recommended)
options.description: The open points are this PR's own doc's § 4 and the review hasn't converged yet. Adds a script and a section; no new backlog item.

options.label: Follow-up PR, new backlog item
options.description: Keeps PR #1173's review scope as it is. Needs a new item ID and its own trace.

questions.question: Should the `..`-above-root probe be sent raw to the real services?

options.label: Yes, expecting a 4xx (Recommended)
options.description: A zero-byte upload under a unique name. If the service resolves the `..`, the script detects that, reports it and deletes the stray object.

options.label: Skip it on cloud
options.description: Probe the escape locally only. What the real service does with it stays undocumented.

questions.question: AWS can't be probed with the current key. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: I'll fix the key, then rerun (Recommended)
options.description: You put a valid key in .env (and add s3express:CreateBucket/CreateSession plus s3express data access on rs-conformance-* if the directory bucket should run). Tell me when, and I rerun s3 and s3express.

options.label: Write up what we have now
options.description: Add the Measured section for Azure HNS plus the local stack now; the AWS rows stay open in § 4 until a later run.

options.label: Drop AWS from this PR
options.description: Record Azure and local only; the S3 open points stay in § 4 as they are.

questions.question: Where should the measured results be written?

options.label: New § in authorities doc + results JSON (Recommended)
options.description: A dated 'Measured' section in research-backend-path-authorities.md, kept separate from the cited authorities, with the probe script and a frozen results JSON under bk-468-key-model/probes/. § 4 shrinks to what is still open.

options.label: Also feed into the key-model doc
options.description: As above, plus a short note in research-key-model.md (§ 3.2 / § 9) that Azure HNS normalises keys server-side and resolves `..` before authorisation, which supports reducing before any key reaches a backend.

questions.question: The two findings above reach beyond this research doc. Should they become backlog items?

options.label: Azurite vs service divergence
options.description: A new item: decide what the Azure conformance tests may assert about raw-key handling, given that Azurite stores keys as sent while the HNS service rewrites them. It needs a new ID and a dossier, in a later PR.

options.label: Azure `..` before authorisation
options.description: A new item: check every raw path to Azure (addressing, `unwrap()`, `native_path`) against a service-side `..` escape under account-wide credentials.

options.label: Neither for now
options.description: The findings stay recorded in § 5 only.

answers.The two findings above reach beyond this: Azurite vs service divergence, Azure `..` before authorisation
